findings.text: The record attributes the plan's ~500-to-340 discrepancy to a window-mean instrument, but the cited prior evidence record contains a 328.9 tok/s window at mean concurrency 23.05 rather than the ~500 tok/s claim, and no repository source contains that figure outside the plan and this new record. The worker manifest itself says explaining ~500 would require the instrument that produced it. The new per-step census disproves 500 in the two parsed logs, but it does not establish what produced the conflicting claim or whether job, prompt mix, pool size or instrument caused the disagreement.

The manifest-named gate receipt begins with a slurmstepd TMPDIR warning and contains only the two summaries plus control result. It has no revision, tree, command or EXIT line, even though the node contract requires those in the receipt. The run stream shows that an earlier invocation emitted the required header and that later srun invocations overwrote the same file; the stream supports all_debug execution and exit zero, but the durable receipt named by the manifest does not.

The 95% intervals resample individual consecutive decode steps as independent observations. These steps come from repeated batches within time-clustered traffic windows, and the report itself notes that all width-29-and-higher observations came from one mid-run window. An IID percentile bootstrap therefore understates uncertainty across workload windows and cannot carry the record's traffic-level flatness adjudication without a block-by-time bootstrap or an explicit statement that the whiskers describe only the empirical per-step distribution.

The evidence commit changes plan-version from 1 to 2 even though the dispatch contract explicitly says not to edit plan-version or plan-modified because concurrent workers make that meta line a merge-conflict hotspot. Every changed path remained inside the file fence, but this line is an explicit within-path scope violation.

justifications.durability: The reducer, full measurement document, figure and two planted-peak fixtures are committed and source readings are bound to byte size and SHA-256. The control is load-bearing for peak selection, but it does not exercise the 20-sample boundary, malformed-line census, operating-band ratio or confidence-interval behavior, and the durable srun receipt lost its header and exit sentinel.
justifications.evidence: The run preserves 79,436 and 1,151 parsed intervals with zero malformed decode lines, all qualifying per-width values, two source digests, a clear two-panel figure and a discriminating planted-peak control; this review reran both committed controls and ruff successfully. Evidence is weakened by the overwritten gate receipt, the unsourced ~500 comparison, and nominal 95% intervals that ignore serial/time-window dependence.
justifications.fit: The driver reuses the existing decode parser, remains under the plan's figure/evidence surface, makes no runtime or lane change and emits portable JSON plus a project-absolute figure reference. The interpretation is appropriately separated from serving code; the main fit qualification is an evidence narrative that over-resolves an unidentified comparison instrument.

The required explanation of why the two earlier claims disagree remains unproved because the source of the ~500-to-340 claim is absent, so the data can reject that level in these logs but cannot attribute its origin.
justifications.scope_discipline: All eight changed paths are within the declared prefixes, the heavy parse ran through all_debug, and the worker made no live service mutation. One explicitly forbidden plan-version edit reduces the score despite otherwise clean scope and commits.
